question: Since the year _______, flame of Amar Jawan Jyoti is continuously burning under the famous monument of India Gate at New Delhi.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Amar Jawan Jyoti was established in 1971 to commemorate the Indian soldiers who died during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.
 
• The eternal flame is located under the India Gate, which is a war memorial located in New Delhi, India.
 
• The flame is symbolic of the nation's gratitude to its soldiers who laid down their lives in service to the nation.
 
• The Amar Jawan Jyoti consists of a marble pedestal with a rifle standing on its barrel, capped by a soldier's helmet, with an eternal flame burning beside it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India Gate:**

 
 
• The India Gate is a war memorial located astride the Rajpath, on the eastern edge of the ceremonial axis of New Delhi, India.
 
• It was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and was built to commemorate the 70,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army who died in the period 1914–21 in the First World War.
 
• The names of 13,300 servicemen, including some soldiers and officers from the United Kingdom, are inscribed on the gate.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pakistani War of 1971:**
 
 
• The Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 was a military confrontation between India and Pakistan that occurred during the Bangladesh Liberation War in East Pakistan.
 
• The war began on 3 December 1971 and lasted for 13 days, ending on 16 December 1971.
 
• The war resulted in the creation of Bangladesh, which was formerly East Pakistan.
 
• The conflict is considered one of the shortest wars in history, and it resulted in a decisive victory for India and the Mukti Bahini.
 
 
 
• **Amar Jawan Jyoti:**
 
 
• The Amar Jawan Jyoti, or the Flame of the Immortal Soldier, is a structure consisting of a marble pedestal with a reversed rifle, capped by a soldier's helmet, and an eternal flame burning beside it.
 
• It was unveiled on 26 January 1972 by the then Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi.
 
• The flame is kept burning day and night to remind the nation of the sacrifice made by its soldiers.
